About 4 years ago I got really into planted aquariums. At this point I always had a few plants in the garden, but I didn't fall in love with plants until aquariums - no idea why. I made a lot of mistakes in the beginning trying to create a 'natural' environment. Plants and fish do work symbiotically, but artificial light and filters are very necessary to make the whole system function (this gets truer the smaller you get). After playing around with a few 10 gallons, I got a 20 gallon for free from a friend. I bout a couple hood lamps and cfls from the hardware store and set the bad-boy up. I started with totally different plants than I have now, but those times are long gone. I originally had 4 minnows, 3 amano shrimp, 1 mystery snail, 1 female beta, many Malaysian trumpet snails, and a few ottocinclus. I bought new zebra danios from the store and with it came some horrible disease. Half the tank died within 24 hours, some fish lost their mouths, the female beta (a rescue) ended up with its mouth sealed shut - it was a nightmare.

As the years have gone on, I just wanted to maintain what I had. Last year I had a baby and so the tank got put on the back burner and moved to a different room. I still feed them and do water changes, but cleaning stopped. You can see [here](http://imgur.com/tOu6NV1) the state I let it get in. And [here](http://imgur.com/4v15N5g) is a good shot of the purple waffle and pothos growing out of the tank.

The only inhabitants left the other day were 3 zebra danios and one died. I came home and it was stuck to the filter. I decided to give the tank some love and risk new fishies. After cleaning the algae up [things stated to look better.](http://imgur.com/etAPMWP)

I went to the store and bought 3 black neon tetras, 3 yellow platys, and a bristle-nosed pleco. I also did some plant trimming and you can see the final result [here.](http://imgur.com/805tXsg). As far as plants I grow amazon sword, wisteria, and red crypts. There is some algae on the lava rocks but I like it there. There is soil in the bottom of the tank to provided nutrients for the plants. Hope you all enjoyed.
